soak-5._comment: Gate measurement, cascaded (overlapping) windows: the last valid run, adeade7 (2026-11-10). Peak 233 MB and growth 27.5 MB: the gate is OPEN. No cascaded 60-minute soak was run on ea9bea4 (owner decision: no further 60-minute soak in this close-out).

note: M4a close-out, Profile ea9bea4 (main 3c53cb5 merged: M5b Deck Terminal in soak-5, M11b, M12). PASS: idle-1 0.077 % / 95 MB, hidden 0.042 % / 71 MB, busy-10 0.70 % / 202 MB, testLaunch 0.309 s / 0.791 s (p90). THE M4a SOAK GATE IS OPEN. Peak: the gate layout is the realistic cascaded (overlapping) one, and its last measurement is 233 MB (adeade7, budget 200): a ~97 MB window-server graphics transient whenever the front window of two overlapping windows changes (soakEvidence); reducing it is a P2 task. The key soak-5 holds that cascaded adeade7 run. The ea9bea4 soak (peak 173 MB, growth 21.3 MB, leaks 0, threads +0, fds +4) was measured with the windows side by side, so its 173 MB peak depends on that layout: it is under soak-5-diagnostic-side-by-side and does not count for the gate. Growth: side by side, 12e43d3 measured 9.1 MB and a84e222 (= ea9bea4's app plus a baseline file) -1.3 MB; ea9bea4's 21.3 MB came from the first cycle landing at minute 10 instead of minute 5 (inside the minute-10 window the metric starts from); a84e222's cycles started at minute 5.0, 10.0, 15.0 ... of sampling, as designed. Leaks 0, threads and fds flat in every run.
build: ea9bea4 (Profile) for soak-5, idle-1, hidden, busy-10 and testLaunch (2026-11-12 02:14-06:40, 1-minute load 1.2-2.9); the later merge of main 64cd2da added only perf/baselines/M12.json. Diagnostic side-by-side soaks: 12e43d3 (2026-11-11 17:54-18:55) and a84e222 (2026-11-12 06:44-07:46).
soakEvidence: A/B of the 97 MB graphics transient ('Owned physical footprint (unmapped) (graphics)'), 15-minute soak-5 runs of 2026-11-11 on the experiment build of 4ef20a9, footprint categories sampled every 0.5 s and aligned with the cycle-phase Darwin notification, screen 1512 x 861 pt visible (14-inch built-in display), samples above 50 MB after the settle: (1) cascaded windows as before (window 2 1100 x 720 at 140,120 over window 1): 82 of 1,819 (4.5 %), every 30 s at window 2's cluster-overview refresh plus 3 per cycle; (2) every NSVisualEffectView inactive and in-window (opaque): 87 of 1,819 (4.8 %), unchanged; (3) windows at the normal level instead of floating (6 min): 29 of 729 (4.0 %), unchanged; (4) -UIDesignRequiresCompatibility / -NSDesignRequiresCompatibility YES (6 min; whether the flag took effect was not verified): 35 of 733 (4.8 %), unchanged; (5) side by side, not overlapping (window 1 at 0,229 and window 2 at 968,229, each 960 x 720, 544 pt of window 2 on screen): 9 of 1,815 (0.5 %), one ~1 s transient per cycle when the cycle opens its Deployments tab. No app code captures windows or renders offscreen. Confound: in (5) window 2 is also 43 % off screen, so less composited area could explain part of the drop; a run with a sliver of overlap, or both windows fully on an external display, would separate the two. Conclusion (a hypothesis: likely, not proven without a minimal two-window control app): a window-server cost of two overlapping app windows, not the app's materials, level or glass. The owner kept the cascaded layout as the gate measurement (real use overlaps windows); side by side is an opt-in diagnostic (-WHPerfSideBySide YES). Reducing the transient is a P2 task. Heap snapshots at cycle lows of the 12e43d3 60-minute run (minutes 10/30/50, live heap 103.4 / 112.9 / 117.2 MB): +5.9 MB is the log ring reaching its 20,000-line cap (flat after minute 30); +0.8 MB the log table's rowCounts cache (pruned only above 2 x lines + 1,000, so it settles near 41,000 entries); JSON store dictionaries flat from minute 30; Swift.StringStorage +3.1 MB, rising about 1.5 MB per 20 minutes after the ring is full (about 4.5 MB/h), NOT attributed: a MallocStackLogging run could not separate it from the first cycle's store cache. Remaining transients: one ~1 s 97 MB graphics blip per cycle (Deployments tab) and +40-60 MB for about 4 s when the cycle opens the Fleet tab and splits it (the fleet refresh decodes the same lists five times because the harness's five clusters are one server). The one-time step after the first cycle (Malloc Small +33 MB, then flat for the next cycles) is attributed to allocator retention as a HYPOTHESIS only (freed small blocks kept dirty for reuse; footprint showed 53-82 MB of Malloc Small as reclaimable at the lows); it was not proven. The a84e222 diagnostic run also showed the cycle's Fleet-and-split phase reaching 304 MB at its 0.5 s maximum (Malloc Small 232 MB, Malloc Large 31 MB, no graphics) for a few seconds; a minute sample landed on it once (213 MB at minute 15).

soak-5-diagnostic-side-by-side._comment: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, not the gate measurement: soak-5 with -WHPerfSideBySide-style non-overlapping windows (the layout was the default on 12e43d3..a84e222 and is now opt-in). The gate measures the cascaded, overlapping layout of real use (key soak-5).
